subject: A loop-head `my` is bound ONCE for the whole loop — a closure made in the body sees the final value (perl gives a fresh instance per iteration)
description:
PRE-EXISTING, found by #297's probes (s385).  Independent of #291: it is identical with the __cond__ rename on or off, and it hits `while` too, which #291 never touches.

REPRODUCERS (perl vs PCL, probed at 20dd3aa and after the #297 fix):
  # (a) C-for condition-my — perl "0,1,2", PCL "3,3,3"
  my @c;
  for (my $i = 0; (my $k = $i) < 3; ++$i) { push @c, sub { $k } }
  print join(",", map { $_->() } @c), "\n";

  # (b) while condition-my — perl "1,2,3", PCL ",," (all undef: the single
  #     binding holds the loop-ending undef)
  my @c; my @l = (1,2,3);
  while (my $x = shift @l) { push @c, sub { $x } }
  print join(",", map { $_->() } @c), "\n";

  # (c) the WORKING contrast — a `my` in the BODY is correct (perl 0,1,2 = PCL):
  for (my $i = 0; $i < 3; ++$i) { my $k = $i; push @c, sub { $k } }
  # ...because the body let is re-entered per iteration.  So the gap is
  # specific to a declaration in the loop HEAD.

CAUSE: `_wrap_cond_mys` puts ONE `(let (($k (make-p-box nil))) …)` AROUND the
whole construct (p-while / p-for), and the head section lowers to a
per-iteration assignment into that one binding.  Every closure made in the body
captures the same binding.  Perl's `my` allocates a fresh pad instance each time
the declaration executes, which is per iteration.

FIX SHAPE (not yet designed): the let must move INSIDE the iteration so it wraps
the condition test AND the body.  For p-while that is
`(loop (let ((k …)) (unless COND (return)) BODY))`; for p-for the STEP must also
see the binding, and `next` must still run the step — check
`make-loop-iteration-body` / the `:next` tag placement before committing to a
shape (a naive let around test+body+step changes what `next` skips).  Needs a
new key on p-while/p-for (e.g. `:head-lex (NAMES)`) rather than a compiler-side
wrap, since only the macro can place a binding inside its own tagbody.

SIZE FIRST: measure how many corpus/suite rows actually close over a head-my
before building it — the cost is a new binding per iteration in every loop that
declares in its head.  Registered in docs/ir-spec.md §6.2 as a known divergence.
